title.narrative: Strengthening community leadership in Technical and Vocational Education and Training and for conflict-affected children and youth in Kachin, Shan, and Kayin States

description.narrative: Contract related to: Strengthening community leadership in Technical and Vocational Education and Training and for conflict-affected children and youth in Kachin, Shan, and Kayin States - On 1 February 2021, the Myanmar military took control of the government, and declared a nationwide State of Emergency. Immediately following the coup citizens organised a nation-wide civil disobedience movement (CDM) and joined large street protests in cities and towns and held nation-wide strikes. Youth activists, specifically Generation Z, have played a major role in organising and leading these protests. The demonstrations were repressed by the military resulting in hundreds of deaths (as of 11th June 861 civilians killed). Many thousands of people have been detained. All government run schools and educational institutions have been closed since the start of the COVID-19 pandemic in March 2020 and there has been no formal learning for an estimated 9.5 million students. Parents and communities have been forced to arrange learning for their children on their own. Many parents are refusing to enrol their children in governmental schools due to safety fears and their support for CDM. Millions of students will be without access to education in the foreseeable future.The Overall Objective (Impact) of this action is to protect Myanmar¿s next generation human capital with education and training. The Specific Objectives (Outcomes) of this action are to:1      Improve access to quality technical and vocational training targeted communities in ethnic and crisis-affected areas;2      Enhance options for online learning and mobility for students and young professionals, who are affected by recent interruptions of university education and employment.Specific Objective 1 of the proposed action will address the current situation where millions of young people have lost access to education and technical and vocational training. Students and youth in ethnic and crisis-affected areas are one of the most vulnerable groups, especially those displaced by conflict and young women and girls. Youth in conflict-affected areas are at higher risk of being trafficked by criminal networks, exploited in harsh, low-paid manual labour, and recruited to fight with little or no training.Specific Objective 2 of the proposed action will address the current situation where an entire generation of students have lost access to formal post-secondary learning. Hundreds of thousands of university students have been unable to pursue higher education or professional development opportunities. Thousands of youth have fled to border areas and neighbouring countries.

title.narrative: Indicator 1: Percentage of young men and women not in education, employment, or training (NEET)

description.narrative: This indicator presents the share of young people who are not in employment, education or training (NEET), as a percentage of the total number of young people in the corresponding age group, by gender. Young people in education include those attending parttime or fulltime education but exclude those in nonformal education and in educational activities of very short duration. Employment is defined according to the OECD/ILO Guidelines and covers all those who have been in paid work for at least one hour in the reference week of the survey or were temporarily absent from such work. Therefore, NEET youth can be either unemployed or inactive and not involved in education or training. Young people who are neither in employment nor in education or training are at risk of becoming socially excluded individuals with income below the povertyline and lacking the skills to improve their economic situation. Young men and women mean aged 1525 in project townships. NEET means those who are not engaged in any form of education, employment, or training. It includes young people who are unemployed, not in school or vocational training, and not seeking employment or training opportunities. Employment is defined according to the OECD/ILO Guidelines and covers all those who have been in paid work for at least one hour in the reference week of the survey or were temporarily absent from such work. Data will be collected through baseline and endline surveys.

title.narrative: 1.1 Percentage of supported young men and women transitioning to employment or selfemployment (by gender, age, and employment pathway) within six months of completing internship or receiving entrepreneurship support

description.narrative: The indicator measures the level of success of employment / selfemployment strategies applied within the project design by measuring to which extent supported men and women were able to find employment or generate selfemployment in the time period of 6 months upon receiving the support from the project. The indicator will be further examined with qualitative elements to determine the level of contribution that the project has had at the endline stage. Young men and women mean aged 1525 in project townships. Supported means that the project supported the youths with TLS, FE and BSD training and after that internship program or productive grant scheme. Transitioning to employment or selfemployment means the youths are successfully employed by local business or successfully forming micro or small business after receiving productive grant. Employment pathway means one of two pathways: employment through internship program or selfemployment through productive grant scheme. Within six months means within or not longer than six months after completing internship or receiving entrepreneurship support (i.e., productive grant scheme.)

description.narrative: The indicator will measure the level of achievement of safety and security standards in terms of learning and working environments with TVET providers and internship hosts engaging with the project. TVET providers are thirdparty private and community facilities that offer training and programs for children and youths in a variety of sectors to secure decent work. Employers (Internship hosts) are local businesses who provide internship programs for youths or employ them. Safe learning and work environments mean an environment that is free from discrimination, harm and abuse and promotes diversity, equity and accessibility for the children and youth. Data will be collected through baseline and endline surveys.

title.narrative: 1.3 Change in qualitative perception of TVET training by parents and students

description.narrative: The indicator will measure the level of perception of quality among the parents and students of the TVET institutions and TVET providers. The baseline will be measured among students and parents of students who report attending a vocational training in the last 6 months. The endline will be collected among the programme beneficiaries who enrolled with the vocational training, regardless of completion status. Change in Qualitative Perception means attitudes and behaviors of parents and students towards TVET training, with an increase in respondents who consider TVET as an option of livelihood creation for themselves or their children. Data will be collected through baseline, midterm review, endline surveys through interviews with children/youth, parents, and other stakeholders. Questionnaire will be designed to gather qualitative data and the questions should be openended and encourage respondents to share their thoughts and opinions. Qualitative data analysis will be applied. Data from baseline survey will be established as a baseline perception and then the proceeding midterm and endline surveys will compare the results from baseline to identify change in perception. Change will be defined based on the scales developed in the questionnaire.

title.narrative: 1.1.4: Number and description of actions included in the community TVET plans by local community

description.narrative: Descriptions of actions will be described in donor reporting as the results of the following processes. Labour market assessment will be conducted. This assessment will inform the following key components of the action: Skills demanded by the corporate actors and small businesses and labour market opportunities, including the anticipated projection of needed skills in line with the industry developments. Gaps in capacities of youth, disaggregating male and female participants (with options for recording nonbinary gender identities) Existing education and TVET opportunities and gaps Barriers for girls and boys, young men and women (including those with nonbinary gender identities) to access existing capacity building opportunities and job opportunities, etc. Income expectations and income achieved in specific targeted sectors. Following the labour market assessment, SCI and coapplicants will engage with TVET SGs to design the township level TVET action plans. These plans will aim to address key gaps identified in the assessment and identify labour market opportunities. Each plan will be codesigned through a series of workshops with TVET SGs that will aim to present the results of the assessment, define strategic priorities, as well as detailed actions to be taken to boost the capacities of youth in the township. A total of 8 TVET plans will be developed, one for each township, to respond to specific contextual elements in each of the targeted areas.

title.narrative: 1.3.3: Percentage of the young men and women who successfully complete selected TVET courses

description.narrative: Young men and women mean aged 1525 in project townships. Type of TVET courses will be defined after local market job assessment and will be specified after the results and shared plan with partners and stakeholders. The project will develop up to three TVET courses to be provided in each of the community learning hubs. Selected means one of the TVET courses selected by young men and women. In total, 3,000 youth will attend TVET courses within the project duration. To avoid youth missing out from the capacity building activities, the courses will be incentivized with small cash stipends for each of the attendees upon completion of the course. The total amount of 60,000 MMK will be provided upon course completion and reception of the course certificate. Successfully complete can be defined by a stipend receipt sheet or reception of the course certificate or training attendance record. Numerator Number of the young men and women who successfully completed selected TVET courses Denominator Number of young men and women enrolled in the selected TVET courses (Output 1.3.1)

description.narrative: Type of TVET courses will be defined after local market job assessment and will be specified after the results and shared plan with partners and stakeholders. The project will develop up to three TVET courses to be provided in each of the community learning hubs. NonTechnical skills courses are Transferable Life Skills, Financial Education and Business Skill Development training. Adapted means curriculums of these courses adapted depending on the results of labor market assessment and then engaging with TVET steering groups, stakeholders, and consultants to meet industry standards and local needs as documented in townshiplevel TVET action plan. A total of 8 TVET plans will be developed, one for each township, to respond to specific contextual elements in each of the targeted areas.

description.narrative: Local business owners means all local business owners in the targeted project area. The project will reach out to industry representatives that can serve as internship hosts. The project will conduct ongoing networking and outreach with private sector and local business to facilitate youth transitions from training cohorts to internships. The project will screen for business owners and invite them to apply for internship hosting. Before the start of each internship, each host will be screened for quality based on the expected number of hours to complete the internship process and the plan for the skills that intern will acquire.

title.narrative: 1.4.4: Number and description of successful workforceemployer networks and labour market practices created through learning hub services

description.narrative: Community learning hub will serve as a community employment hub that will provide networking service for trained youth and the employers. Current labour market practices for labour search is that most businesses rely on their personal and family network, and rarely can find technical capacities in their surroundings. The networking activity will ensure that youth with demanded capacities are adequately presented to the potential employer, as well as that the job and the employer are adequately presented to the youth. The project will map out unemployed youths who completed the TVET courses and their capacities. The database will be managed by the CLH staff. The networking activities may include but are not limited to conducting Job fairs with participation of targeted youth and local businesses, organizing Business Caf networking events, etc. The number and description of networking activities and established activities will be reported in donor reporting. The data can be collected through case studies, interviews and FGD.
